records.title: Binance CEX — Frontend & Infrastructure
records.chain: Ethereum, Bitcoin, TRON, Avalanche, Optimism, Arbitrum, Base
records.description: Binance CEX exploited via Key Leaked via Infrastructure. Loss $6,360,000,000.

raw.name: Binance CEX
raw.description: On October 29, attackers exploited Binance’s operational infrastructure to execute unauthorized withdrawals across multiple blockchains, resulting in approximately $6.3 billion in losses. Binance’s preliminary investigation identified a potentially compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that allowed access to a service container, with no evidence of wallet private key leakage. Approximately $3 billion in stolen assets were later frozen with help from industry partners. Binance committed to covering all losses using its SAFU fund and company reserves

records.title: Bitget — Key Compromise
records.description: Bitget exploited via Hot Wallet Key Compromised. Loss $387,000,000.

raw.name: Bitget
raw.description: Bitget detected unauthorized transfers involving a limited number of hot wallets at 18:31 UTC on September 24. Subsequent tracing identified approximately $387.5M transferred to attacker-controlled addresses across Ethereum and other EVM networks, XRP Ledger, Zcash and Tron. Bitget states that the incident has been contained and no further unauthorized transfers are possible

records.title: Liquid Network — Bridge & Cross-Chain
records.description: Liquid Network exploited via Unbacked Cross-Chain Mint. Loss $320,000,000.

raw.name: Liquid Network
raw.description: An actor exploited a software vulnerability in Elements, the software underlying Liquid, to create approximately 4,000 L-BTC without corresponding BTC backing. The unbacked L-BTC was transferred to SideSwap’s peg-out service, where it was indistinguishable from legitimately backed L-BTC. SideSwap processed a valid peg-out and burned the L-BTC, causing the Liquid Federation to release approximately 3,996 BTC from its Bitcoin reserves. Liquid and SideSwap state that SideSwap’s Peg-out Authorization Key and the federation’s other keys were not compromised

records.title: Tectonic — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Tectonic exploited via Donation Attack. Loss $124,470,000.

raw.name: Tectonic
raw.description: The attacker built a leveraged TONIC/tTONIC collateral position through 98 recursive operations, then transferred TONIC directly into the tTONIC contract twice without minting corresponding tTONIC, increasing the tTONIC exchange rate outside the normal deposit path. The attacker also increased TONIC’s market price, while Tectonic’s price feed relied on VVS Finance and Crypto.com Exchange pricing without smoothing or a circuit breaker. These effects compounded the collateral valuation, allowing the attacker to borrow and remove more than $120M of assets from Tectonic’s lending markets within roughly 11 minutes

records.title: Ledger (Supply Chain) — Frontend & Infrastructure
records.description: Ledger (Supply Chain) exploited via Supply Chain Attack. Loss $93,000,000.

raw.name: Ledger (Supply Chain)
raw.description: Attackers purchased genuine Ledger hardware wallets, installed concealed components capable of capturing recovery phrases, and redistributed the modified devices through resellers. The implants monitored the wallets’ displays during initialization and transmitted captured recovery phrases through cellular connections. Attackers subsequently derived users’ private keys and drained their cryptocurrency holdings. Ledger confirmed that its Secure Element, operating system, and internal infrastructure were not compromised

records.title: Nesa — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Nesa exploited via Arithmetic Error. Loss $50,000,000.

raw.name: Nesa
raw.description: Nesa was exploited through a Cosmos EVM vulnerability involving inconsistent balance accounting between Cosmos EVM and the Cosmos SDK. In the shared exploit mechanism documented by Cosmos Labs, delegation of locked tokens from a vesting account through the staking precompile could cause an unchecked EVM balance underflow to approximately 2^256. The resulting artificial balance could then be used to overflow a high-balance victim account, reducing the victim balance to zero while transferring its legitimate tokens to the attacker, with no net increase in token supply. Nesa has confirmed exploitation of a Cosmos EVM vulnerability but has not publicly disclosed its Nesa-side exploit transaction or victim account, so application of the exact shared mechanism to Nesa remains strongly supported but not independently demonstrated at transaction level

records.title: Mercado Bitcoin — Protocol Logic
records.chain: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, TRON, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, BSC, Stellar, XDC
records.description: Mercado Bitcoin exploited via Unknown. Loss $40,000,000.

raw.name: Mercado Bitcoin
raw.description: On November 2, 2026, attackers compromised a system at Mercado Bitcoin and transferred more than $40 million in crypto from exchange-associated wallets across various blockchains. The exchange contained the incident and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while investigating the transfers. Tether froze more than $4.5 million USDT associated with the theft. Mercado Bitcoin stated that customers would not incur losses and that no customer data was exposed

records.title: CoinDCX — Key Compromise
records.description: CoinDCX exploited via Hot Wallet Key Compromised. Loss $16,000,000.

raw.name: CoinDCX
raw.description: CoinDCX experienced approximately $16 million in suspicious outflows from TRON addresses associated with its exchange infrastructure. The exchange attributed the incident to addresses compromised during its July 2025 security breach, which continued receiving deposits after being deprecated. CoinDCX acknowledged that its deposit-sweeping process failed temporarily and stated that it absorbed the resulting losses while crediting affected users. Investigators disputed whether the addresses had genuinely been removed from active operations

records.title: Lighter Perps — Frontend & Infrastructure
records.description: Lighter Perps exploited via API Key Compromised. Loss $10,393,057.

raw.name: Lighter Perps
raw.description: On November 16, 2026, an attacker exploited a leaked API key belonging to a trader on Lighter, enabling unauthorized activity that resulted in the withdrawal of approximately 10.39 million USDC from the platform. The stolen funds were transferred to an attacker-controlled Ethereum wallet, exchanged for ETH through CoW Swap, and partially routed to Hyperliquid. Lighter confirmed that its protocol and smart contracts were not compromised, temporarily suspended withdrawals and liquidity pool creation, and activated Guardian mode to prevent further unauthorized withdrawals. An additional attempted withdrawal remained under investigation, with the full scope and recovery status unconfirmed

records.title: KiiChain — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: KiiChain exploited via Arithmetic Error. Loss $9,700,000.

raw.name: KiiChain
raw.description: An attacker exploited chained balance-accounting defects in the shared Cosmos EVM module used by KiiChain. By deploying a contract at a precomputed vesting-account address and delegating one wei more KII than its spendable balance, the attacker triggered an arithmetic underflow in the staking precompile’s EVM balance write-back. Combined with a missing overflow guard in the EVM value-transfer path, this allowed real KII to be redirected from victim accounts to attacker-controlled addresses without increasing total supply. The sequence was repeated against 18 targets

records.title: Moonwell Lending — Oracle Manipulation
records.description: Moonwell Lending exploited via Spot Price Manipulation. Loss $8,700,000.

raw.name: Moonwell Lending
raw.description: The attacker manipulated the spot price of the relatively illiquid MAMO token, increasing the collateral value recognized by Moonwell. The attacker used the inflated MAMO collateral to borrow liquid assets including cbBTC, ETH/WETH, USDC, and wstETH, leaving the lending markets with undercollateralized positions

records.title: TermFinance Vaults — Governance
records.description: TermFinance Vaults exploited via Malicious Proposal. Loss $8,500,000.

raw.name: TermFinance Vaults
raw.description: An attacker acquired majority voting power in the thinly held governance tokens controlling Term Vaults and used that voting power to pass malicious governance proposals. The proposals gave the attacker control over the affected vaults, enabling the underlying assets to be withdrawn. The attack therefore did not require stealing an administrative key or bypassing an authorization check—the attacker obtained the required authority through the governance mechanism itself. Recent reporting indicates the affected products were Term’s strategy vaults built on Yearn V3 infrastructure rather than Term Finance’s core fixed-rate repo lending architecture

records.title: TAC — Protocol Logic
records.description: TAC exploited via Withdrawal Logic Flaw. Loss $7,500,000.

raw.name: TAC
raw.description: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the shared Cosmos EVM precompile layer and transferred 2,985,651,403 TAC from a single account to another account without authorization. TAC states that the incident was a drain rather than a mint: no new TAC was created and total supply remained unchanged. The network was halted at block 24,671,475 to contain the incident

records.title: Duelbits — Key Compromise
records.description: Duelbits exploited via Hot Wallet Key Compromised. Loss $7,000,000.

raw.name: Duelbits
raw.description: Duelbits suffered unauthorized transfers from hot wallets across Ethereum, BSC, Bitcoin, and Tron. Stolen assets were rapidly moved, bridged and largely consolidated into ETH and DAI on Ethereum. Duelbits took its platform offline while investigating and stated that user funds were safe. Security researchers suspect compromise of hot-wallet private keys, but Duelbits has not yet published a technical root cause

records.title: Astroport — Governance
records.description: Astroport exploited via Malicious Proposal. Loss $4,900,000.

raw.name: Astroport
raw.description: Neutron governance proposal 9 contained MsgUpdateAdmin messages that reassigned administration of Astroport contracts despite those contracts previously being administered by Astroport’s own governance contract. After the proposal passed, the attacker migrated Astroport Staking and six Astroport pair contracts to attacker-uploaded code containing a withdraw_all entry point and swept their balances. The attack did not exploit Astroport’s swap or pool logic

records.title: X100 — Governance
records.description: X100 exploited via Flashloan Governance Attack. Loss $4,750,000.

raw.name: X100
raw.description: X100’s governance system allowed an attacker to obtain two of three Senate seats using flash-loan-funded X tokens. The attacker immediately used this majority to approve and execute a malicious treasury proposal within the same transaction. The proposal forced the Freezer to swap 400,000 X tokens into an attacker-controlled liquidity pool with zero minimum output, allowing the attacker to extract treasury value through a manipulated trade

records.title: Drop — Governance
records.description: Drop exploited via Malicious Proposal. Loss $4,400,000.

raw.name: Drop
raw.description: Neutron governance proposal 9 reassigned administration of Drop’s dATOM converter and withdrawal-manager contracts to the attacker. After the proposal passed, the attacker migrated both contracts to previously uploaded malicious code exposing a withdraw_all function and swept their entire balances. Drop’s liquid-staking or redemption logic itself was not exploited; the contracts were taken over through Neutron chain governance

records.title: Gamdom — Frontend & Infrastructure
records.chain: Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Solana, TRON, Bitcoin
records.description: Gamdom exploited via Key Leaked via Infrastructure. Loss $4,208,000.

raw.name: Gamdom
raw.description: Gamdom suffered a multichain hot-wallet compromise following unauthorized access to an automation server. Investigators traced approximately $4.21M in stolen assets across eight networks. The attacker subsequently bridged, swapped, and distributed funds through multiple wallets and services, including Mayan, Hyperliquid, and THORChain. The precise mechanism used to obtain control of the wallets remains unconfirmed

records.title: NEAR Intents — Bridge & Cross-Chain
records.description: NEAR Intents exploited via Bridge Logic Flaw. Loss $3,800,000.

raw.name: NEAR Intents
raw.description: NEAR Intents was exploited through a bug in the interaction between its Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure and the NEAR Intents smart contract, allowing unauthorized withdrawals. The team stopped services, patched the contract-side vulnerability, and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals across multiple networks while completing fixes to the Omni infrastructure. The stolen funds were traced toward KuCoin and then BTC, and NEAR Intents said the losses would be compensated in full

records.title: Kava Lend — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Kava Lend exploited via Arithmetic Error. Loss $3,700,000.

raw.name: Kava Lend
raw.description: On November 14, 2026, attackers exploited an arithmetic flaw in Kava Lend's BUSD market that allowed its supply interest index to increase approximately 243,000-fold when calculated against an extremely small effective supply. The attackers used the resulting inflated collateral claims to repeatedly borrow KAVA, then liquidated the loans through a process that erased the debt without recovering sufficient collateral. Approximately 53.9 million KAVA, worth $3.7 million before the subsequent market selloff, was stolen from the lending protocol. The attackers bridged and sold much of the stolen KAVA on BNB Chain, while approximately 612,416 USDT in laundering proceeds was blocked at the Relay bridge

records.title: Nostra Money Market — Oracle Manipulation
records.description: Nostra Money Market exploited via Spot Price Manipulation. Loss $3,500,000.

raw.name: Nostra Money Market
raw.description: An attacker manipulated the price of NSTR in an illiquid onchain market, causing the manipulated price to enter NSTR’s Pragma oracle response. The attacker then used NSTR at the inflated valuation as collateral in Nostra’s money market to borrow approximately $3.5M of other assets. Pragma says NSTR had limited liquidity and source coverage, the affected oracle response had only two contributing sources, and the manipulated input reflected an onchain pool price rather than a decimals or median-calculation error. Nostra paused its money market following the incident

records.title: Nomic — Bridge & Cross-Chain
records.description: Nomic exploited via Unbacked Cross-Chain Mint. Loss $3,150,000.

raw.name: Nomic
raw.description: A vulnerability in Nomic’s custom forwarding mechanism allowed an attacker to double-spend nBTC and generate false cross-chain vouchers that were sent to Osmosis. These vouchers resulted in unbacked nBTC entering Osmosis and becoming part of Alloyed BTC’s backing. Osmosis and IBC were not compromised. After detecting the issue, Osmosis froze Nomic and Alloyed BTC inflows and outflows and coordinated an emergency upgrade with validators that froze 22.65 BTC in the attacker’s address

records.title: Fogo Foundation — Key Compromise
records.description: Fogo Foundation exploited via Private Key Compromised. Loss $3,000,000.

raw.name: Fogo Foundation
raw.description: An unknown actor compromised the Fogo Foundation and transferred 400M FOGO tokens to an attacker-controlled destination. Fogo has not disclosed the specific attack vector, affected Foundation wallet, or how authorization over the tokens was obtained. The Fogo blockchain itself was not initially compromised; the network was subsequently halted as a precaution to prevent movement of the affected tokens and upgrade the network to restrict associated addresses

records.title: Polymarket International — Frontend & Infrastructure
records.description: Polymarket International exploited via Supply Chain Attack. Loss $2,700,000.

raw.name: Polymarket International
raw.description: Attackers reportedly compromised a third-party website monitoring service used by Polymarket, allowing malicious JavaScript to execute on its international trading platform. The script hijacked authenticated trading sessions to sell prediction-market positions and transfer assets to attacker-controlled wallets. Polymarket temporarily suspended trading, removed the affected integration, and committed to reimbursing impacted users

records.title: Initia — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Initia exploited via Infinite Mint. Loss $2,600,000.

raw.name: Initia
raw.description: Initia suffered a security incident involving the unauthorized minting of multiple assets on its L1. The attacker reportedly transferred and converted some of the minted assets into Ethereum-based holdings. Initia halted its L1 and rollups while investigating the vulnerability and coordinating with validators, exchanges, and security teams

records.title: Aquifer — Access Control
records.description: Aquifer exploited via Arbitrary External Call. Loss $2,469,729.

raw.name: Aquifer
raw.description: Aquifer allowed the caller to supply the input-side token program used during swaps instead of pinning it to the canonical SPL Token Program. The attacker supplied a malicious program that accepted Aquifer’s CPI transfer instruction and returned success without transferring the required input tokens. Aquifer failed to verify the actual input-token balance increase and consequently released real output tokens from its vaults without receiving payment

records.title: Arcus Perps — Protocol Logic
records.description: Arcus Perps exploited via Withdrawal Logic Flaw. Loss $2,234,391.

raw.name: Arcus Perps
raw.description: On November 10, 2026 (UTC), an attacker exploited an accounting flaw in Arcus Perps on Robinhood Chain that allowed transfers between subaccounts to artificially inflate an account's recorded balance. The attacker used the inflated balance to withdraw 2,234,391 USDG, while an additional $3 million in withdrawal requests was blocked by the bridge's rate limit and later reversed. Arcus patched the vulnerability, restricted the exploiter's accounts, and covered the entire shortfall from its company treasury, leaving user balances unaffected

records.title: Fake GIWA Bridge — Social Engineering
records.description: Fake GIWA Bridge exploited via Impersonation Scam. Loss $2,080,000.

raw.name: Fake GIWA Bridge
raw.description: Scammers deployed a counterfeit OP Stack-style network impersonating GIWA, including an RPC endpoint, Ethereum bridge and batch-posting infrastructure. The fake network reported GIWA’s expected mainnet Chain ID 9134, causing DYORSWAP and users to mistake it for the legitimate GIWA mainnet. Users voluntarily deposited ETH into the fraudulent bridge. After accumulating deposits, the scammers drained 766.25 ETH to an attacker-controlled address. GIWA’s actual mainnet had not launched, and neither GIWA nor DYORSWAP’s smart contracts were exploited

records.title: Payy Network — Bridge & Cross-Chain
records.description: Payy Network exploited via Bridge Logic Flaw. Loss $1,828,589.378.

raw.name: Payy Network
raw.description: Payy’s RollupV1 bridge processed a malicious verifyRollup batch containing an unauthorized 1,828,589.378132 USDC withdrawal to the attacker alongside ordinary withdrawals. The batch was submitted using Payy’s prover and validator infrastructure. ExVul reports that the malicious withdrawal had an all-zero burn hash that users cannot normally generate through Payy’s public circuits, indicating that the forged withdrawal entered during proving or aggregation rather than through an ordinary user withdrawal. Payy has confirmed the bridge exploit but has not yet established whether the cause was compromised prover/validator credentials or a proof-aggregation verification flaw

records.title: Limit Break Payment Processor — Access Control
records.description: Limit Break Payment Processor exploited via Token Approval Abuse. Loss $1,800,000.

raw.name: Limit Break Payment Processor
raw.description: A vulnerability in Limit Break’s Payment Processor allowed an attacker to abuse users’ existing token and NFT approvals to transfer assets without a legitimate marketplace purchase. Payment Processor V2 on Ethereum was exploited first, and V3 contained the same vulnerability. Limit Break paused V3 where possible, while whitehats transferred vulnerable NFTs to safe custody because V2 could not be paused and ApeChain V3 could not immediately be paused. The same underlying approval flaw could be used in reverse against WETH approvals, resulting in 660 WETH being stolen along with other tokens before whitehats could secure it

records.title: Notional V2 — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Notional V2 exploited via Arithmetic Error. Loss $1,727,782.

raw.name: Notional V2
raw.description: An attacker exploited an unchecked uint128 cast in Notional V1’s collateral valuation logic. By minting two fCash positions against the same payer with notionals of 1 and 2^128-1, the attacker engineered a debt balance of exactly 2^128. When the free-collateral check converted the debt to ETH, uint128(balance.abs()) truncated 2^128 to zero, making the insolvent payer appear to have no debt. The attacker then settled the fabricated fCash claims and withdrew approximately $1.73M in USDC and DAI from the Escrow

records.title: Fetch.ai — Key Compromise
records.description: Fetch.ai exploited via Private Key Compromised. Loss $1,530,000.

raw.name: Fetch.ai
raw.description: Fetch.ai’s TokenConversionManagerV3 conversionIn() relied on an ECDSA signature from a single authorizer as its principal authorization mechanism. After obtaining that authorizer’s private key, the attacker signed a fresh conversion message for an attacker-controlled recipient and called conversionIn(). Unlike conversionOut(), the function lacked the checkLimits(amount) restriction and did not independently require proof that corresponding assets had been burned or locked on the other side of the conversion. The valid signature was therefore sufficient to release the converter’s entire remaining FET inventory in one transaction

records.title: Qubic — Key Compromise
records.description: Qubic exploited via Weak Key Generation. Loss $1,300,000.

raw.name: Qubic
raw.description: An attacker exploited predictable wallet seeds generated with insufficient randomness in Qubic’s wallet software, compromising 1,404 user wallets and stealing approximately 2.94 trillion QU. The vulnerability affected certain wallets created on Apple devices and Safari browsers. Qubic halted its network at tick 85,371,949, while MEXC froze the account receiving the remaining stolen funds. Seed generation was corrected in wallet version 4.26.4

records.title: Papertrade — Oracle Manipulation
records.description: Papertrade exploited via Spot Price Manipulation. Loss $1,280,000.

raw.name: Papertrade
raw.description: Papertrade, a perpetual trading protocol on HyperEVM, reportedly suffered an oracle manipulation attack shortly after launch. The attacker manipulated Hyperliquid’s ETH order-book midpoint through external trades while opening and closing highly leveraged synthetic positions on Papertrade. Because the protocol used the instantaneous BBO midpoint without TWAP, deviation limits, or independent price validation, manipulated prices were accepted for execution and PnL settlement, transferring approximately $1.28M from the Martingaler LP

records.title: Radix — Access Control
records.description: Radix exploited via Improper Access Control. Loss $1,249,946.

raw.name: Radix
raw.description: A Radix Engine execution-layer flaw allowed transactions to obtain direct references to arbitrary internal fungible and non-fungible vaults without verifying that the caller owned or was authorized to access them. The attacker supplied internal vault addresses to custom code and directly invoked withdrawal functionality, bypassing the authorization rules of the accounts and components holding those vaults. Across 26 transactions, the attacker drained nearly the entire Radix supply of six Hyperlane-wrapped assets and then used their normal Hyperlane Warp Routes to bridge the stolen assets out of Radix

records.title: Affluent — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Affluent exploited via Unbacked Mint. Loss $1,053,000.

raw.name: Affluent
raw.description: Affluent’s lending vaults reportedly suffered unauthorized share minting that allowed attackers to redeem vault assets without providing corresponding deposits. The supplied analysis identifies suspicious transactions on September 30, October 12, and October 16, 2026, involving multiple wallets. Extracted assets were reportedly transferred through exchanges, swaps, and cross-chain services

records.title: Fence Finance — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: Fence Finance exploited via Incorrect Share Accounting. Loss $1,010,000.

raw.name: Fence Finance
raw.description: An attacker exploited a tranche vault associated with Fence Finance and Valinor Digital by using a flash loan to obtain an inflated allocation of vault shares. The attacker subsequently redeemed those shares to withdraw approximately $1.01 million in USDC from the vault

records.title: Bloom Trading Bot — Frontend & Infrastructure
records.description: Bloom Trading Bot exploited via Supply Chain Attack. Loss $953,000.

raw.name: Bloom Trading Bot
raw.description: An attacker exploited a reported remote code execution vulnerability in a third-party software module used by Bloom’s trading infrastructure, enabling unauthorized transfers from user wallets. Approximately 9,408 SOL was drained from 48 wallets belonging to nine traders within 94 seconds. Bloom attributed the incident to the third-party module and denied that private keys were exposed, while Bitquery confirmed that the transactions were signed using the affected wallets’ keys

records.title: Sovryn Lend — Protocol Logic
records.description: Sovryn Lend exploited via Unknown. Loss $914,000.

raw.name: Sovryn Lend
raw.description: On October 31, 2026, attackers exploited Sovryn's lending and margin contracts on Rootstock through three transactions, extracting approximately $914,000 in XUSD and WRBTC. Sovryn paused its core protocol and lending pools after detecting the incident. A 24-hour withdrawal delay enabled the team to block seven additional withdrawals totaling approximately 66,134 XUSD before the funds reached the attackers. The underlying vulnerability remains undisclosed while the team completes security repairs and reconciles affected positions

records.title: Virtue — Oracle Manipulation
records.description: Virtue exploited via Oracle Misconfiguration. Loss $894,500.

raw.name: Virtue
raw.description: An attacker exploited Switchboard’s IOTA guardian-attestation design to replace the signing keys of all 14 production oracles and submit arbitrary IOTA prices. The attacker first inflated IOTA to $10M, allowing 4.94M unbacked VUSD to be minted against 1.027 IOTA, then crashed the reported price to trigger liquidations of healthy positions. By pre-positioning the freshly minted VUSD in Virtue’s Stability Pool, the attacker captured 16.72M IOTA-equivalent of collateral from the manipulated liquidations

records.title: zkLink Nova — Bridge & Cross-Chain
records.description: zkLink Nova exploited via Cross-Chain Message Spoofing. Loss $783,100.

raw.name: zkLink Nova
raw.description: An attacker exploited zkLink’s Arbitrator contract, which failed to clear a previously authenticated message hash after processing a claim. By reusing that hash through the publicly accessible SyncL2TxHashRelayer, the attacker impersonated an authorized gateway message and installed a malicious L2 logs root. The attacker then submitted forged withdrawal proofs against the compromised root to drain approximately $783,100 from zkLink’s Ethereum bridge

records.title: Ajna V2 — Protocol Logic
records.description: Ajna V2 exploited via Liquidation Logic Flaw. Loss $775,400.

raw.name: Ajna V2
raw.description: Attackers exploited Ajna’s internal liquidation accounting across multiple lending pools. Current on-chain analysis shows liquidation operations could be sequenced to extract collateral while returning insufficient quote assets to the pool, including bucketTake, collateral removal, take, and settlement operations

records.title: Chainflip AMM — Bridge & Cross-Chain
records.description: Chainflip AMM exploited via Bridge Logic Flaw. Loss $736,442.17.

raw.name: Chainflip AMM
raw.description: An attacker exploited Chainflip’s TRON-specific swap instruction and refund handling. Unlike Chainflip’s other integrations, TRON swap instructions were derived from transaction memos. The attacker could attach a different memo to a transaction already signed by Chainflip validators, causing Chainflip to interpret the transaction as another swap. When that duplicate instruction failed, the protocol refunded it even though the underlying deposit had already produced a payout, effectively allowing the same deposit to be paid twice. The attacker attempted the sequence eight times over approximately 90 minutes, with six unauthorized payouts succeeding

records.title: CometDEX — Token & Share Accounting
records.description: CometDEX exploited via Incorrect Share Accounting. Loss $717,000.

raw.name: CometDEX
raw.description: CometDEX’s Soroban AMM allowed same-asset swaps such as USDC→USDC. When token_in and token_out were identical, the contract loaded two independent copies of the same reserve record, added the input amount to one copy and subtracted the output from the other, then wrote both back to the same map key. The second write overwrote the first, causing the pool’s recorded reserve to fall below its actual token balance. The attacker then deposited against the understated reserve, received excess LP shares, and redeemed those shares for real pool assets. The cycle was repeated 36 times using flash liquidity. Blend contracts themselves were not exploited, but Blend Backstop depositors were exposed because the backstop held BLND/USDC Comet LP shares

records.title: The Sandbox — Access Control

raw.name: The Sandbox
raw.description: The Sandbox’s SAND cross-chain bridge was exploited after an attacker abused approveAndCall on the Base SAND OFT contract to hijack LayerZero delegate permissions. The attacker changed trusted cross-chain configuration, minted unbacked SAND on Base and BNB Chain, and used the compromised bridge path to extract approximately 14.75M backed SAND from the Ethereum OFT adapter. The Sandbox disabled bridging on Base and BNB Chain and stated that SAND on Ethereum and Polygon was unaffected at the token-contract level

raw.name: Initia
raw.description: On November 10, 2026, an attacker used compromised rollup infrastructure keys to fabricate IBC transfers and withdraw assets from escrow accounts on Initia's Layer 1 that held funds bridged to multiple rollups. records.title: Flamincome — Oracle Manipulation
records.description: Flamincome exploited via Spot Price Manipulation. Loss $595,000.

raw.name: Flamincome
raw.description: Flamincome’s VaultYUSDT strategy valued its Convex-staked Curve USDP LP position using the strategy’s BaseRewardPool.balanceOf() multiplied by Curve’s spot get_virtual_price(). The attacker used approximately $18M USDT of Morpho flash liquidity to acquire USDP and imbalance-mint USDP metapool LP, then permissionlessly staked LP for the strategy through Convex. This temporarily increased the strategy’s reported holdings/NAV. VaultYUSDT immediately incorporated the manipulated valuation into its share price, allowing the attacker to redeem shares at an inflated value and force the strategy to withdraw real aUSDT liquidity from Aave

records.title: TENDRIL — Protocol Logic
records.description: TENDRIL exploited via Swap Logic Flaw. Loss $550,000.

raw.name: TENDRIL
raw.description: On November 5, 2026, an attacker exploited TENDRIL's token sell logic to drain approximately 550,000 USDT from its PancakeSwap V2 liquidity pool on BSC. Each sell triggered PoolControl.sellToken(), which called TENDRIL.controlburn() to burn tokens directly from the liquidity pair and synchronize its reserves before the seller's remaining tokens arrived. The attacker used flash-loan-funded transactions to exploit the resulting reserve imbalance and withdraw nearly all the pool's USDT liquidity. ExVul estimated the attacker's campaign profit at no more than 181,910 USDT after observed purchases and gas costs, excluding an unresolved LP-position basis

records.title: MakerDAO ETH-A Liquidation Keeper Bot — Access Control
records.description: MakerDAO ETH-A Liquidation Keeper Bot exploited via Improper Access Control. Loss $538,000.

raw.name: MakerDAO ETH-A Liquidation Keeper Bot
raw.description: A dormant third-party MakerDAO ETH-A liquidation keeper had an unprotected drain routine that lacked ds-auth authorization. Any caller could invoke the function and provide the withdrawal recipient. The attacker triggered Flipper.deal() for four auctions the keeper had won in 2020, causing 200 WETH of previously unclaimed collateral to move through Vat.flux to the keeper, then used GemJoin.exit() to send it to an attacker-controlled recipient and unwrap it to ETH. MakerDAO’s core contracts behaved as designed; the vulnerability was in the third-party keeper

records.title: NuNet — Key Compromise

raw.name: NuNet
raw.description: An attacker possessing NuNet’s deployer/mint authority directly called mint() on the NTX token and created 408,532,878.13 unbacked NTX in a single mint.
